Sugriva Wrestles Ravana on the Roof

Stories from the Ramayana

Sugriva Wrestles Ravana on the Roof

A wrestling match on the palace roof — and a fallen crown

In everyday English — Yuddha Kanda, sarga 40

Stories by Eku

How to Read · · BEFORE WE BEGIN

Read it out loud. This story is made to be told. Read slowly, as if you are sitting with everyone at home.

This book is the war's first clash — but no sword was drawn, no arrow shot. Two kings — Sugriva and Ravana — wrestle with their hands. Where there is a leap, raise your voice; where there is wrestling, read slowly, holding your breath.

The yellow boxes hold the characters' own words. Change your voice a little as you speak them — Sugriva fearless, Ravana furious, Rama laughing.

(Purple hints) tell you where to pause, whisper, or raise your voice. They are for the reader — do not read them aloud.

The green box at the end of each part — Pause and think. Stop there. Ask questions. Let the listeners speak.

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sarga 40 — Sugriva's duel with Ravana on the roof. Anything more you may want to know is given separately at the end, in Where This Story Comes From.

Who's Who · · WHO'S WHO

Sugriva — king of the vanaras, Rama's friend. A mighty vanara hero, fearless, skilled in wrestling. The hero of this book.

Ravana — king of Lanka. Tall, dark-complexioned, black moustache, tall golden crown, a single head, royal robes. Standing on the roof of his palace.

Rama — prince of Ayodhya, archer. Warm dark-brown skin, fully clothed. Watching the duel from below with his army.

Lakshmana — Rama's younger brother, beside him at every step.

The vanara army — the army halted on Mount Suvela, watching the duel from below.

1 · Ravana on the Palace Roof · · RAVANA ON THE PALACE ROOF

Morning had come. The vanara army was halted on Mount Suvela — and preparations for war were going on before Lanka.

Ravana had climbed to the roof of his palace — the roof of the tall palace, from which all of Lanka and the shore of the sea could be seen.

He stood there looking at the army — lakhs of vanaras, flags, boulders, trees. Pride was on his face — “My Lanka cannot be breached — what can these vanaras do?”

Down in the army stood Sugriva too. He looked up — and saw Ravana standing on the roof.

Sugriva said — “Look! Ravana stands on the roof — alone, without guards. He watches us — as if we were a game.”

A thought came into Sugriva's mind — a thought that had come into no one else's mind.

Pause and think — Ravana stands on the roof looking at the army — from a height, with pride. Is looking from a height also pride? And Sugriva looks at him from below — is seeing from below different from seeing from above?

2 · Sugriva's Leap · · SUGRIVA'S LEAP

Sugriva planted his feet on the ground — gathered his body — and in a single leap sprang upward!

He flew through the air — from the foot of Mount Suvela, over the walls of Lanka — and landed straight on the roof of Ravana's palace!

Ravana was startled — before him, on his own roof, stood the king of the vanaras!

Sugriva said — “Ravana! I am Sugriva — king of the vanaras, friend of Rama. You stood on the roof watching us — now I stand before you.”

Ravana clenched his fists in anger — “Vanara! How dare you — you have come onto my roof!”

Pause and think — Sugriva reaches the roof in a single leap — is that only strength — or courage? And when the enemy comes onto the roof of your own house — whom does fear strike — him, or you?

3 · The Wrestling · · THE WRESTLING

The two looked at each other — and then they grappled! No sword, no bow, no arrow — only hands, only strength.

Ravana seized Sugriva — Sugriva seized Ravana. They spun each other around, pushed, tried to throw each other down. The roof shook — the palace trembled.

Ravana was mighty — he had defeated many gods. But Sugriva was no less — he was king of the vanaras, a lifter of mountains.

They circled on the roof — now Ravana on top, now Sugriva on top. Below, the army watched — the vanaras holding their breath, the rakshasas astonished.

Sugriva said — “Ravana! I have seen your strength — now see mine!”

Ravana said — “Vanara! You will not escape my hands!”

Pause and think — Two kings wrestle — without weapons. Is fighting without weapons more bravery — or less? And when both are equal — whose is the victory — strength's, or the heart's?

4 · The Crown Falls · · THE CROWN FALLS

The wrestling went on — and then a moment came. Sugriva seized Ravana's hand — spun him around — and with his other hand snatched at Ravana's head!

In his hand came Ravana's crown — the tall golden crown, the sign that Ravana was king!

Sugriva hurled the crown down with force — it spun through the air and fell — and landed on the earth of Lanka!

Below, the vanaras saw — Ravana's crown lies in the dust! The vanaras cheered — “Victory to Sugriva! Victory to Rama!”

Sugriva said — “Ravana! Your crown has fallen — your pride will fall just the same!”

Pause and think — The crown falls — but Ravana does not fall. Is the falling of a crown itself defeat? And when a king's crown lies in the dust — whose is that dust — the crown's, or the king's?

5 · Sugriva's Return · · SUGRIVA'S RETURN

Ravana went mad with anger — his crown had fallen, he had been insulted. He reached out to seize Sugriva —

But Sugriva in a single leap sprang down from the roof — flew through the air — and landed on Mount Suvela, beside Rama!

Ravana was left standing alone on the roof — without his crown, trembling with anger.

Below, the vanaras surrounded Sugriva — “My king! You have knocked down Ravana's crown!”

Pause and think — Sugriva fights and returns — unhurt. Is returning also a victory? And Ravana is left alone on the roof — is being left alone itself defeat?

6 · Rama's Laughter · · RAMA'S LAUGHTER

Rama looked at Sugriva — and laughed. A laughter that rang through the morning before the war.

Rama said — “Sugriva! What you did — no one else could have done. You went to Ravana's roof — you wrestled him — and you knocked down his crown!”

“It is not only a crown that has fallen — it is the first defeat of Ravana's pride.”

Lakshmana smiled — Sugriva bowed his head — “My lord, all this is by your grace.”

Over in Lanka, Ravana sat in his palace — the crown lay in the dust, and for the first time a thought rose in his mind — “Can I lose?”

Pause and think — Rama laughs — laughter before a war. Can laughter also be strength? And when Rama praises Sugriva — whose victory is that praise — Sugriva's, or friendship's?

7 · The War's First Personal Duel · · THE WAR'S FIRST PERSONAL DUEL

Evening was falling. On Mount Suvela the army was ready — and in the palaces of Lanka there was silence.

This was the war's first clash — between two kings, face to face, with their hands. No army, no weapons — only two heroes.

And in this clash a crown fell — Ravana's crown. The crown lying in the dust on Lanka's earth — as if saying — “Pride falls — dharma stands.”

Rama called his captains — “From tomorrow morning the siege begins.”

But that story — is in the next book.

Pause and think — In the first clash no one died — only a crown fell. Is winning without killing also victory? And the falling of the crown — is it the beginning of the war — or does it tell the end of the war in advance?

Where This Story Comes From · · WHERE THIS STORY COMES FROM

Main Source

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sarga 40 — Sugriva's duel with Ravana on the roof.

Ravana on the Palace Roof — Sarga 40

Ravana standing on his palace roof looking down at the vanara army below; Sugriva seeing him — this is in sarga 40.

Sugriva's Leap — Sarga 40

Sugriva reaching the palace roof in a single leap and challenging Ravana — this is in sarga 40.

The Wrestling — Sarga 40

The two wrestling hand to hand without weapons — seizing, spinning, pushing — this is in sarga 40.

The Crown Falls — Sarga 40

Sugriva tearing off Ravana's crown and hurling it down; the crown falling in the dust — this is in sarga 40.

Sugriva's Return — Sarga 40

Sugriva leaping back to Rama's side; Rama laughing and praising him — this is in sarga 40.

About the Pictures

Wrestling is shown in this book — but no wounds, no blood, no death. The pictures show the leap, the wrestling and the falling crown — the duel is told only in words.

What Happens Next

Now Angada will go as envoy to Ravana's court — and then the armies will clash. Angada's story is in the next book of this series.
